quizzes.title: Pax Silica and Critical Minerals: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: Critical minerals and advanced technology have become matters of strategic planning. A United States-led multilateral framework, Pax Silica, aims to build a secure, resilient and innovation-oriented global technology ecosystem, and India is set to join it. The framework is designed to counter vulnerabilities in critical technology supply chains and to reduce over-dependence on coercive or unreliable sources. Its key objectives include minimising strategic vulnerabilities arising from concentrated supply chains, safeguarding sensitive and emerging technologies from misuse, and promoting secure, interoperable and trusted technology networks among partner countries. Its scope covers semiconductors, AI infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, compute and data logistics. Within India, the National Critical Minerals Mission seeks to enhance domestic exploration, reduce import dependence and develop processing and recycling capabilities. The mission also encourages public sector and private companies to acquire mineral assets abroad, aims to enhance trade with resource-rich countries, and lists regulatory and financial support among its key objectives. A dedicated body, Khanij Bidesh India Ltd, is responsible for identifying and acquiring overseas assets related to critical minerals. Exploration is also extended to the Indian Ocean seabed under the Samudravaan Project, which is aimed at finding critical minerals there. The mission also lists processing and recycling capabilities and overseas mineral acquisitions among its key objectives.

questions.q: Which ministry is the nodal ministry for the National Critical Minerals Mission?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Ministry of Mines as the nodal ministry for the mission.

questions.q: In which district is India's first lithium site, Salal-Haimana, located?
questions.explanation: The booklet places Salal-Haimana in Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.q: Which state hosts India's first lithium auctioned site?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Korba in Chhattisgarh as the first lithium auctioned site.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Israel is one of the members of Pax Silica.
Reason (R): Singapore is one of the members of Pax Silica.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but Singapore's membership does not explain Israel's membership.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Minerals Security Partnership   ->   A. Five lithium brine blocks in Argentina
II. Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology (iCET)   ->   B. Argentina, Bolivia and Chile
III. Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL)   ->   C. Only developing-country member: India
IV. Lithium triangle   ->   D. Semiconductors, AI and wireless communication
questions.explanation: The Minerals Security Partnership has India as its only developing member, iCET covers semiconductors, AI and wireless communication, KABIL acquired five brine blocks in Argentina, and the lithium triangle is Argentina, Bolivia and Chile.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The National Critical Minerals Mission runs from FY 2020-21 to 2025-26.
II. The United Kingdom is one of the members of Pax Silica.
III. A law enacted in 1957 enables mining concessions for critical minerals.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because the mission runs from FY 2024-25 to 2030-31, while II and III are stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Minerals Security Partnership was launched in 2022.
II. The Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology was launched by India and the US in 2024.
III. Japan is one of the members of Pax Silica.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while iCET was launched in 2022, not 2024.

quizzes.title: Pax Silica and Critical Minerals: TITA practice
quizzes.passage: India is set to join a United States-led multilateral framework called Pax Silica, which seeks to build trusted technology supply chains. Its scope covers semiconductors, AI infrastructure, critical minerals and energy inputs, advanced manufacturing, and compute and data logistics. Member countries include the United States, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, the United Kingdom and Israel, along with other like-minded technology partners. The framework aims to reduce over-dependence on coercive or unreliable sources and to safeguard sensitive technologies from misuse. Its trusted digital infrastructure objective promotes secure, interoperable technology networks among partner countries, and it seeks to minimise strategic vulnerabilities arising from concentrated supply chains. Within India, the National Critical Minerals Mission seeks to enhance domestic exploration, reduce import dependence and develop processing and recycling capabilities. The mission also supports overseas acquisitions of mineral assets by public sector and private companies, and it aims to enhance trade with resource-rich countries. A dedicated body, Khanij Bidesh India Ltd, is responsible for identifying and acquiring overseas assets related to critical minerals. Exploration is also extended to the Indian Ocean seabed under a separate project. The mission's key objectives further include regulatory and financial support, along with overseas acquisitions and processing capabilities. Advanced manufacturing also covers high-end hardware within the framework's scope.

questions.q: Apart from Argentina and Chile, which country forms part of the lithium triangle? (country)
questions.explanation: The lithium triangle comprises Argentina, Bolivia and Chile.

questions.explanation: The booklet names the Ministry of Mines as the nodal ministry.

quizzes.title: Schemes and Governance Platforms: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: Government schemes in India address goals as varied as tourism, skill training, maternal health and urban livelihoods. Swadesh Darshan is a central sector scheme that aims at the integrated development of theme-based tourist circuits. Its major circuits include the Buddhist, Heritage, Eco-Tourism, Himalayan, Coastal and Desert circuits. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana provides short-term skill training, upskilling and recognition of prior learning to young people. Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, and candidate records are kept on the Skill India Portal. A CAG audit of the scheme found that training programmes were not adequately aligned with actual labour market needs, and that many certified candidates possessed only basic literacy despite job roles that required technical education. The same audit noted duplicate bank accounts and identical photographs among candidate records. A separate scheme gives a conditional cash transfer to pregnant women and lactating mothers to improve maternal health and nutrition. Beneficiaries must register their pregnancy, complete at least one ante-natal check-up and have an institutional delivery. Governance platforms also play a role in delivery. One such platform tracks the status of mega projects, their timelines and bottlenecks, and the Prime Minister's Office provides overall oversight of it. Its coordination role spans several agencies and ministries.

questions.q: In which year was Swadesh Darshan launched?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Swadesh Darshan was launched in 2015.

questions.q: According to the CAG audit of PMKVY (2015-2022), what share of funds released for state components remained unspent?
questions.explanation: The audit found that nearly 20% of funds released for state components remained unspent.

questions.q: Under which umbrella scheme was PMMVY incorporated in 2022?
questions.explanation: The booklet says PMMVY was incorporated into Mission Shakti in 2022.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): PRAGATI is a platform for monitoring and grievance redressal.
Reason (R): PRAGATI integrates with CPGRAMS to address citizens' grievances.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the CPGRAMS integration is the reason PRAGATI addresses grievances.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. PRASHAD   ->   A. Affordable working capital loans for street vendors
II. Swadesh Darshan 2.0   ->   B. Conditional cash transfer for pregnant women and lactating mothers
III. PM SVANidhi   ->   C. Infrastructure at major pilgrimage and heritage sites
IV. PMMVY   ->   D. Destination-centric and sustainable tourism
questions.explanation: PRASHAD funds pilgrimage and heritage site infrastructure, Swadesh Darshan 2.0 is destination-centric, PM SVANidhi offers working capital loans, and PMMVY is a conditional cash transfer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The PMKVY audit found that the placement rate was only 41 per cent.
II. PM SVANidhi was launched in 2015.
III. PRAGATI is a two-tier platform.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since PM SVANidhi was launched in 2020 and PRAGATI is a three-tier platform.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. PMMVY targets pregnant women and lactating mothers aged 19 years and above.
II. Swadesh Darshan 2.0 shifted from destination-centric to circuit-based infrastructure.
III. About 95 per cent of PMKVY candidate records had invalid or missing information.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while Swadesh Darshan 2.0 shifted from circuit-based to destination-centric infrastructure.

quizzes.title: Schemes and Governance Platforms: TITA practice
quizzes.passage: India runs many schemes that combine cash support, skill training and infrastructure. Swadesh Darshan is a central sector scheme of the Ministry of Tourism that develops theme-based tourist circuits, and its second version moves towards destination-centric and sustainable tourism, with a focus on environmental sustainability and local community participation. PRASHAD focuses on infrastructure at major pilgrimage and heritage sites. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, run by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, gives short-term skill training to youth and recognises prior learning. An audit by the CAG of this scheme found weak planning, unspent funds, data gaps and poor placement outcomes. A conditional cash transfer scheme supports pregnant women and lactating mothers, and it aims to improve maternal health and nutrition. PRAGATI is a monitoring platform that tracks mega projects and their timelines, and it integrates with CPGRAMS for grievances. Union government secretaries coordinate between central ministries under it, while chief secretaries of states ensure implementation at the state level. PM SVANidhi offers affordable working capital loans to street vendors, so that they can resume livelihoods, and that objective relates to disruptions caused by COVID-19 lockdowns. It is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs together with the Department of Financial Services.

questions.q: In which year was Swadesh Darshan launched? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Swadesh Darshan was launched in 2015.

questions.q: In which year was PMMVY incorporated into Mission Shakti? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says PMMVY was incorporated into Mission Shakti in 2022.

questions.q: How many tiers does the PRAGATI platform have? (number, in words or digits)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes PRAGATI as a three-tier monitoring and grievance redressal platform.

questions.q: What percentage of candidate records in the PMKVY audit had invalid or missing information? (per cent, number only)
questions.explanation: The audit found that around 95 per cent of candidate records had invalid or missing information.

questions.q: What placement rate did the PMKVY audit find? (per cent, number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the PMKVY placement rate was only 41 per cent.

questions.q: Which ministry is the nodal ministry for PMMVY? (ministry name)
questions.answer: Ministry of Women and Child Development
accept: Ministry of Women and Child Development
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Ministry of Women and Child Development as the nodal ministry for PMMVY.

questions.q: What is the minimum age, in years, of PMMVY beneficiaries? (years)
questions.explanation: PMMVY targets pregnant women and lactating mothers aged 19 years and above.

quizzes.title: Defence, Diplomacy and Resources: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: India and Germany have a strategic partnership now spanning a quarter century, and the German Chancellor's first official visit to India was held to mark that milestone. The visit also comes ahead of the upcoming 75 years of diplomatic relations between the two countries. The two countries signed agreements covering defence, trade, technology, mobility and Indo-Pacific engagement. In defence, a joint declaration of intent was signed to develop a roadmap for defence industrial cooperation, with focus areas that include co-development and co-production of defence platforms. Germany also expressed interest in taking part in Indian naval and air exercises, including the air combat exercise Tarang Shakti, and in activities connected with the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium. The education agenda includes the Indo-German Comprehensive Roadmap on Higher Education, and academic collaboration, skill development and research mobility are priorities. Business travel and academic exchanges are to be promoted. The visit took place in Gujarat, and the partnership's broader cooperation covers climate, education and research. A green and sustainable development partnership aligns bilateral climate cooperation with the Paris Climate Agreement goals, with focus areas such as renewable energy, climate finance and sustainable development. An Indo-German Science and Technology Centre supports research, development and industrial innovation, and the partnership also covers people-to-people ties.

questions.q: In which year was the Indian Peacekeeping Force (IPKF) withdrawn from Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the IPKF was withdrawn in March 1990.

questions.q: Which organisation brokered the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960 with the World Bank as broker.

questions.q: Which European organisation partners with DRDO for the Eurodrone MALE UAV programme?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that DRDO partners with Europe's OCCAR for the Eurodrone programme.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India and Pakistan exchange lists of their nuclear installations every year.
Reason (R): Bilateral trade between India and Germany crossed USD 50 billion in 2024.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the India-Germany trade figure does not explain the nuclear list exchange.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Pinaka LRGR-120   ->   A. Gandhinagar, Gujarat
II. Sawalkot hydropower project   ->   B. Long-range artillery weapon system
III. Eastern rivers   ->   C. Full rights to India
IV. German Chancellor's first official visit   ->   D. 1856 MW run-of-river project on the Chenab
questions.explanation: Pinaka is a long-range artillery weapon system, Sawalkot is a 1856 MW project on the Chenab, the eastern rivers have full rights for India, and the Chancellor's visit was in Gandhinagar.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Operation Pawan was launched to enforce peace and disarm militant groups in Sri Lanka, primarily the LTTE.
II. The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1991.
III. The Pinaka LRGR-120 was flight-tested at Chandipur, Odisha.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960, while I and III are stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Germany announced a visa-free transit facility for Indian passport holders.
II. The Indo-Sri Lanka Accord was signed on 29 July 1987.
III. The India-Pakistan agreement on nuclear installations was signed on 31 December 1990.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while the India-Pakistan agreement was signed on 31 December 1988.

quizzes.title: Defence, Diplomacy and Resources: TITA practice
quizzes.passage: India and Germany have a strategic partnership that the German Chancellor's first official visit to India was held to celebrate. The visit took place in Gujarat and led to agreements on defence, trade, technology, mobility and Indo-Pacific engagement. The partnership's focus areas include technology partnerships and co-development and co-production of defence platforms. Germany announced a visa-free transit facility for Indian passport holders, and both countries seek to promote business travel and academic exchanges. In defence, DRDO works with a European organisation on the Eurodrone unmanned aerial vehicle programme. India has also developed a long-range guided rocket system called Pinaka for its army. It is a long-range artillery weapon system developed for the Indian Army. That rocket system was flight-tested from a test range, and its development involved several research laboratories. India is accelerating a hydropower project in Jammu and Kashmir called Sawalkot amid renewed tensions over the Indus Waters Treaty. A 1960 treaty governs the rivers shared with Pakistan, while the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej are fully available to India. India and Pakistan also exchange lists of their nuclear installations every year under an agreement that prohibits attacks on such facilities. The partnership also includes a green and sustainable development agenda that is aligned with the Paris Climate Agreement goals.

questions.q: In which year did the India-Pakistan agreement on nuclear installations enter into force? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the agreement, signed in 1988, entered into force on 27 January 1991.

questions.q: What is the approximate range, in km, of the Pinaka LRGR-120? (km)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the range of Pinaka LRGR-120 as approximately 120 km.

questions.q: On which river is the Sawalkot hydropower project located? (river)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Sawalkot project is a 1856 MW run-of-river project on the Chenab river.

questions.q: In which Indian state is the Chandipur test range, where Pinaka was flight-tested? (state)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Pinaka test took place at Chandipur's Integrated Test Range in Odisha.

questions.q: For how many years has the India-Germany strategic partnership been in place, as marked during Chancellor Merz's first visit? (years)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the visit marked 25 years of the India-Germany strategic partnership.

questions.q: Operation Pawan was launched after which accord signed on 29 July 1987? (accord name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Operation Pawan was launched following the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord signed on 29 July 1987.

questions.q: Which organisation brokered the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960? (organisation)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Indus Waters Treaty was brokered by the World Bank.
